Alcohol makes you sleepy because ` [Highlight start] it acts as a central nervous system depressant that slows brain activity and triggers calming brain chemicals [Highlight end] `.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgQEBxCJF17jbujxNR8UyvQsquo2t8_9SrtxtUneoPePCHdwwSqMb4bQr9nVYWMBbdPrp7cXi5ON3ExGjhnbZla73nPmGPoCqeN5TxcTZlHJaPQiH_AieBz8WFLl50nFwvDSmtCfw_RrxiAge2m43he_o6gIq12T2FayfB4VwOY51PCU)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHEIkXXIZi1tHAGc31RnbLwVJmKrZDAWvw8v0ZPG8bLuSpTglJI5oklcglpAcALKWbpgZirKSzNZIIZ-YDwWBND9C0UwtcoPucU-viy42eojNXqFc07ui7taqeQLlLH6XOXIVOepixB1pfhW5n1w40gXDj7Lz2I)

### Why It Causes Drowsiness

- **Slows brain activity:** Ethanol slows the central nervous system, reducing alertness and reaction speed.
- **Boosts GABA:** It increases gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), a neurotransmitter that calms the brain and promotes relaxation.
- **Lowers glutamate:** It suppresses glutamate, an excitatory chemical that normally keeps you awake and focused.
- **Amplifies existing fatigue:** Drinking on an empty stomach, drinking quickly, or already being tired or slightly sleep-deprived can make the drowsy effect hit harder.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdwHEIkXXIZi1tHAGc31RnbLwVJmKrZDAWvw8v0ZPG8bLuSpTglJI5oklcglpAcALKWbpgZirKSzNZIIZ-YDwWBND9C0UwtcoPucU-viy42eojNXqFc07ui7taqeQLlLH6XOXIVOepixB1pfhW5n1w40gXDj7Lz2I)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgQEBxCJF17jbujxNR8UyvQsquo2t8_9SrtxtUneoPePCHdwwSqMb4bQr9nVYWMBbdPrp7cXi5ON3ExGjhnbZla73nPmGPoCqeN5TxcTZlHJaPQiH_AieBz8WFLl50nFwvDSmtCfw_RrxiAge2m43he_o6gIq12T2FayfB4VwOY51PCU)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESewHEIkXXL_h5G0-dLSYHZ3Wo5Z1tBrXS5WVYW7EU393OK5LUB8Wdh4apTRxaamXEWJW0jgfx_UmGR35K45rBzGZawjUD_b6VV9ObtxOWRigFwHNIKcmCXOxoxGRJse5D4SlJjKc7JNXR86g4vl-6sOzzBJ8tHtOMe21PSg)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESegHEIkXX7jcpyQqhGTzvgTDrRQg49QrCHsxpF75WaN8lP6I4nruSf-0qMjQ5zFnc4Z3VW3yL7amabChWHUwXgW8hkPeQLmz6xiB8xdxr07MEnxVu9c4IWaR1fLjymrCf96JduTQVAOMxM0xZo0lJcQCKgFpcAeXzKqi5)

### What Happens Later

Even though a drink can help you drift off faster, it often disrupts sleep quality later on. As your body metabolizes the alcohol—usually a few hours later—it can suppress REM sleep, relax throat muscles, increase nighttime bathroom trips, and cause rebound wakefulness. [Verywell Health](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgQEBxCJF17jbujxNR8UyvQsquo2t8_9SrtxtUneoPePCHdwwSqMb4bQr9nVYWMBbdPrp7cXi5ON3ExGjhnbZla73nPmGPoCqeN5TxcTZlHJaPQiH_AieBz8WFLl50nFwvDSmtCfw_RrxiAge2m43he_o6gIq12T2FayfB4VwOY51PCU) explains how these brain chemical shifts and sleep stage changes work, while [Harvard Health](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESegHEIkXX7jcpyQqhGTzvgTDrRQg49QrCHsxpF75WaN8lP6I4nruSf-0qMjQ5zFnc4Z3VW3yL7amabChWHUwXgW8hkPeQLmz6xiB8xdxr07MEnxVu9c4IWaR1fLjymrCf96JduTQVAOMxM0xZo0lJcQCKgFpcAeXzKqi5) covers how alcohol's sedative and rebound effects lead to fatigue and nighttime awakenings. [Healthline](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgQEBxCJF1-qePcWSsbhTp8RAxT_DOMaS-ECGiohJyjNbtI-NwKF3Adv9pXZQVdtQI_OXYiNgrU5lG53zE5LqPLtEhfXlQvAkeBtB51LXR3sp3Pov_AWSF0Q_077LJcueCrvU-B80f7TOdJTyUT_j_L5Mi4tsZ9sterRPStsePghtqLc) also notes why alcohol isn't a reliable sleep aid and highlights practical tips for sleeping after drinking.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgQEBxCJF1-qePcWSsbhTp8RAxT_DOMaS-ECGiohJyjNbtI-NwKF3Adv9pXZQVdtQI_OXYiNgrU5lG53zE5LqPLtEhfXlQvAkeBtB51LXR3sp3Pov_AWSF0Q_077LJcueCrvU-B80f7TOdJTyUT_j_L5Mi4tsZ9sterRPStsePghtqLc)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgQEBxCJF17jbujxNR8UyvQsquo2t8_9SrtxtUneoPePCHdwwSqMb4bQr9nVYWMBbdPrp7cXi5ON3ExGjhnbZla73nPmGPoCqeN5TxcTZlHJaPQiH_AieBz8WFLl50nFwvDSmtCfw_RrxiAge2m43he_o6gIq12T2FayfB4VwOY51PCU)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkwEBxCJF11CaSTkCQLUmN0EBjrbMtqNICV3MgWaai8KL-ore_6Yy0VwlicO_LhqEIj3YGp8qBxKA7NxMGKK5iW4wqe9XXfEyvWINO4t-k730DUEaz0pdThbDvxdybe7-GgXFcjoEuQEgFJVucoNqdTjAtiWdWvJvQUlf88LPnTy3AyshGtGEnzxKqtZKQx51Ef17_e4)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESegHEIkXX7jcpyQqhGTzvgTDrRQg49QrCHsxpF75WaN8lP6I4nruSf-0qMjQ5zFnc4Z3VW3yL7amabChWHUwXgW8hkPeQLmz6xiB8xdxr07MEnxVu9c4IWaR1fLjymrCf96JduTQVAOMxM0xZo0lJcQCKgFpcAeXzKqi5)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESeQHEIkXXtEkcca6JwyRmno84ZuWldYGO7LNf-DY2K715KQuQcUyKeHx3HwcWFihrg2ypt70bEXf3jIV-USwP7ZLqs4uRuRcY919LbIN8wod4FHr2PfRlacVyaKcSlk9CyOEhA4iQ_vFNIu8yHd9mFg5H3zn8bXL-eQc)Are you asking because you get **sleepy right after a drink** , or because you **wake up tired** the next day?
